children: Norway’s general public domestic loan debt rose by 4.5% year-on-year to NOK 8.05 trillion at the end of August 2026, following an eight-month low of 4.3% growth in the previous month.
Lending growth to non-financial corporations increased to 4.8% from 4.0%, reaching NOK 2.42 trillion, while household loan growth remained steady at 4.6%, totaling NOK 4.79 trillion.
In contrast, municipal government loan debt growth eased to 3.0% from 3.4% a month earlier, reaching NOK 8.38 billion.
On a seasonally adjusted annualized one-month basis, total loan debt for the general public grew by 5.3%, following a 3.8% increase in the prior period.

title: Norway Loan Debt Rises 4.5% in August
